messages:
Alex M.: Heads-up — NorthEdge wants a firm p95 p99 SLA for their payments routing use case. Sales pushed for p95=150ms / p99=450ms. I ran a quick canary and saw p95 ~140ms but p99s spiking to 1.1s under bursts.
Priya S.: Do we know which kernel path they hit? small-batch vs fused attention?
Alex M.: Profiling shows most hot requests use the quantized kernel on A100 with small sequences. The tail correlates with KV-cache misses & kernel fallback to non-quant path during cold-start microbursts.
Samir K.: Can you paste the perf snippet?
Alex M.: Sure — here’s the tail window from the canary: 
```
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z request_id=nx-42 latency_ms=112 p50
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z request_id=nx-43 latency_ms=146 p95
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z request_id=nx-44 latency_ms=1450 p99
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z note=kv_cache_miss model_path=quant_v2 kernel=quant_fallback
```
Priya S.: That 1.45s looks like a KV warmup + kernel swap sequence. If we can pre-warm KV or pin microbatching we can cut that down.
Erica L.: Microbatch sizing matters here. Right now runtime uses adaptive microbatch with max 8. For low-concurrency customer threads, that introduces delays when we force synchronous execution to avoid kernel swap.
Samir K.: Tradeoff: increase baseline microbatch to 4 to amortize overheads vs risk of added queueing latency for p95.
Jordan (Sales): From Sales — NorthEdge will only accept the SLA if we can justify the p99 path. They also asked about cost delta if we pin resources to avoid falls. Need a short summary to send.
Alex M.: Proposed mitigation options: 
- KV pre-warm on cold start + sticky routing for a minute (drops p99 in tests from 1.45s -> ~360ms)
- Force quantized kernel only pipeline + disable fallback (reduces tail but can add errors for some tokens)
- Raise reserved microbatch min to 4 (improves throughput but p95 edges up ~10-20ms in our sim)
- Customer-dedicated warm pool (best latency, ~30% extra infra cost)
Priya S.: Add measured numbers: pre-warm -> p95 150ms p99 380ms, disable fallback -> p95 142ms p99 290ms but regen quality risk ~0.6% per eval set, microbatch=4 -> p95 160ms p99 420ms.
Jordan (Sales): That's great. Can you put that in one line for exec/contract: "Option A: pre-warm + sticky routing — p95=150ms p99=380ms, minimal code change. Option B: dedicated warm pool — p95=140ms p99=260ms, +30% infra. Option C: disable fallback — p95=142ms p99=290ms, risk: small quality regressions."
Samir K.: Also note: kernel selection heuristic fix in #PR-334 cuts KV misses by avoiding unnecessary kernel probes. If we ship that, the microburst p99 drops ~120ms on average. Recommend we include "pending runtime patch" caveat.
Erica L.: I pushed a short patch to lower the probe frequency; can run another canary at 11:00. DeployBot: rolling canary for eng-runtime/runtime@staging -> prod canary group 7.
DeployBot: canary started: 2155551250.
Alex M.: OK schedule: run patch canary -> re-run NorthEdge scenario -> collect p95/p99 + token-level quality evals -> send summary to Jordan by EOD. Anyone object?
Priya S.: No objections. I'll prepare the quality delta numbers.
Jordan (Sales): Perfect — with those we can offer a split SLA: p95 guaranteed at 150ms, p99 best-effort with defined mitigations and optional premium dedicated pool.
Samir K.: Quick reminder for contract wording: "p99 best-effort" is fine, but add a clause about acceptable microbursts and request patterns (e.g., spikes >200 rps per customer are excluded).
Alex M.: Agreed. I'll draft the short note for sales with the three options + expected cost delta and the pending kernel fix.
Jordan (Sales): Thanks — ping me when the draft is ready and I'll loop legal/procurement. :thumbsup:
Erica L.: Canary finished: DeployBot reports success for canary group 7. Perf collector shows p99 reduced to ~350ms in repeat run (without dedicated pool).
Alex M.: Nice. I'll update the summary with the new numbers and close the loop.
Jordan (Sales): Awesome — will wait for the doc.
